correctness.rationale: With infinite square graph, midpoint-to-vertex unit magnetic incidence B, all finite-support zero modes have u=0 because B* u=0 propagates zeros along infinite connected graph. Each occupied support edge has nonzero amplitude and Bz=0 implies occupied degree >=2. For <=6 edges connected square-grid minimum-degree-two subgraphs are elementary 4-cycles or six-edge 2-square perimeters, consistent exactly when holonomy t^area=1. For t generic neither, and the seven-edge theta graph of adjacent squares supports explicit h=(-t,1,t,-t²), v=(t,-(1+t),1) satisfying all six vertex balances. For generic t its minimal 7-edge topology must be the two-adjacent-unit-face theta; the incidence matrix has rank six when t≠1, so unique state up to gauge and scalar. Six edge amplitudes have modulus 1 and one |1+t|; hence IPR (6+q²)/(6+q)², q=|1+t|²; Cauchy-Schwarz gives exact 1/7 iff q=1, equivalently cos(phi)=-1/2. Boundary t=-1 reduces to six edges, t=1 supports elementary square. Independently checked balance and IPR at six phases. The global support cutoff comes from graph-cycle argument, not finite-patch enumeration.
